tiles.heading: 01 · LOOK HERE FIRST — THREE TO FIVE LONG COMBS
tiles.details: Follow ONE attached flowering culm from rooted bunch to its head. Tall grama commonly bears 3–5 fairly straight or gently curved, one-sided pectinate branches 2.5–4.5 cm long. Branch counts and height overlap hairy grama; the existing whole-plant panels teach silhouette but do not prove the species-level terminal anatomy.
tiles.short: Robust perennial; usually 3–5 combs about 25–45 mm long
tiles.status: PUBLISHED FIELD CUE — CONNECTED MEASURED CULM NEEDED

tiles.heading: 02 · OPEN THE TRUE COLLAR
tiles.details: At the INNER blade–sheath junction expose the short ciliate/hairy ligule separately from marginal blade hairs. Published 0.2–0.5 mm ligule hairs in the broad hairy-grama complex are COMPARISON CONTEXT, not a measured B. pectinata threshold. Obtain a 1-mm-scale collar photo from the same vouchered flowering plant.
tiles.short: Check the actual hair-fringed ligule; do not borrow a numeric length

tiles.heading: 03 · EXAMINE THE COMB'S FAR TIP
tiles.details:
Flora field cue (Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas, p. 1248) — Inspect the point past the last full spikelet with a hand lens. The Flora describes it as a reduced spikelet, usually forked at its tip and hairy at its base.

The regional North Central Texas key describes a reduced, axis-like terminal spikelet beyond the ordinary crowded spikelets, often hairy basally and forked at the tip. This is NOT automatically the simple naked rachis extension ('stinger') often emphasized for B. hirsuta. Photograph a mature undamaged tip side-on at 10–20× with 1-mm ruler before arrowing either structure.

Photo still needed: a side view of the entire pointed tip, with the fork and the hairs at the base of the reduced spikelet in focus.
tiles.short: Look for an axis-like terminal rudimentary spikelet, hairy at base and often bifid

tiles.heading: 04 · ISOLATE ONE FERTILE AND STERILE FLORET
tiles.details: Separate a ripe spikelet from ONE identified comb. Identify both outer glumes, the lower bisexual fertile lemma/palea, and the reduced upper sterile floret and its awns. Broad B. hirsuta-complex accounts describe ~5–6 mm spikelet bodies, but this is NOT a validated species-specific measurement for B. pectinata; measure the actual specimen and do not include awns in body length.
tiles.short: Each crowded spikelet has a lower fertile floret and reduced upper sterile floret

tiles.heading: 05 · MEASURE GLUMES, LEMMAS AND AWNS
tiles.details: Comparison-only B. hirsuta-complex descriptions report lower glume ~1.4–3.5 mm, upper glume ~3–6 mm, fertile lemma ~2–4.5 mm, and short fertile-lemma awns; reduced sterile lemmas may carry three longer awns. None of those ranges is independently established for the distinct B. pectinata concept. Photograph each organ with 1-mm scale and label awn ORIGIN, not just a distant bristly outline.
tiles.short: Use the dissected same-plant spikelet; complex measurements are provisional

tiles.heading: 06 · SEPARATE HAIRY, BLUE AND TEXAS GRAMAS
tiles.details: Hairy grama (B. hirsuta) can overlap in branch number and share a projecting tip; compare the actual terminal rudiment, basal hair placement and mature spikelets. Blue grama (B. gracilis) usually has 1–3 curved eyebrows; Texas grama (B. rigidiseta) has many much shorter (~10 mm) bristly units; red grama has slender appressed branches. Historical B. hirsuta varieties and possible hybrid intermediates require careful voucher review. The hairy-grama panel is a LOOK-ALIKE, not tall-grama anatomy.
tiles.short: Compare same-scale combs and terminal tips, not color or branch count alone
tiles.status: COMPARISON LESSON — MATCHED TIP MACROS NEEDED

steps.title: 1 · First, recognize the plant
steps.look_for: Start with the ROBUST bunchgrass and often THREE TO FIVE relatively LONG straight or slightly curved pectinate combs near the top of a flowering culm. One mature branch may extend beyond its spikelets as a bare axis. This can overlap hairy grama; measure the complete heads, count branches on ONE culm, and inspect basal hair and distal rudimentary spikelet morphology.
steps.why_it_matters: Start with the recorded recognition characters before making a species identification.

steps.title: 2 · Examine the whole plant
steps.look_for: First inspect the archived upright tuft and tall stems, then follow the multiple comb-bearing culms in the second view. Finally use the hand-scale comb image for branch profile; none resolves individual florets.
steps.why_it_matters: Habit and growing context are supporting evidence, not proof of hidden roots or rhizomes.

steps.title: 3 · Inspect leaves, collar and nodes
steps.look_for: At the INNER blade–sheath junction expose the short ciliate/hairy ligule separately from marginal blade hairs. Published 0.2–0.5 mm ligule hairs in the broad hairy-grama complex are COMPARISON CONTEXT, not a measured B. pectinata threshold. Obtain a 1-mm-scale collar photo from the same vouchered flowering plant.
steps.why_it_matters: Examine the real structures; the photo may not expose or measure all the described characters.

steps.title: 4 · Check the flowering structure
steps.look_for: Comparison-only B. hirsuta-complex descriptions report lower glume ~1.4–3.5 mm, upper glume ~3–6 mm, fertile lemma ~2–4.5 mm, and short fertile-lemma awns; reduced sterile lemmas may carry three longer awns. None of those ranges is independently established for the distinct B. pectinata concept. Photograph each organ with 1-mm scale and label awn ORIGIN, not just a distant bristly outline.
steps.why_it_matters: Use an attached, correctly identified specimen when deciding the flower or spikelet structures.

steps.title: 5 · Compare similar grasses
steps.look_for: TALL GRAMA B. pectinata is usually robust with 3–5 often relatively long straight combs; B. hirsuta has pronounced branch hairs and bare 'stinger' but can overlap in branch count and rachis tip. Blue grama mostly 1–3 curved eyebrows, spikelets tending to extend to branch tip; Texas grama very short woolly/awned groups; red grama thin wiry small appressed racemes. Avoid a species diagnosis from size or branch count alone.
steps.why_it_matters: Confirm at least two independent botanical characters; do not remove a native candidate from color alone.

panels.label: UVALDE CC0 REFERENCE — habitat and elevated culms
panels.caption: Real Uvalde thin-soil limestone habitat with long nearly upright flowering culms rising above a sparse short prairie grass layer; individual stems overlap with other plants, and the photographer's species ID is not an independently vouchered same-plant rooted specimen. No specific belowground root/crown structures or true leaf collars resolve at this image scale.

panels.caption: Follow the whole comb toward the pale, pointed end at the upper right. The Flora identifies the point as a reduced spikelet. This photo shows where to look. A sharper close-up is needed to see the fork and basal hairs described in the Flora.

memory_rule: Find the full mature flowering stem; count only combs attached to it and photograph the root crown for scale.
safety_note: Do not claim microscopic glumes/ligule/awn count from these macroscopic views. Taxon IDs follow recorded source determination; native status unchanged.
